title: enrichment image format not accepted
body:
for several, but not all pdfs that i am indexing, i get the following error

> Skipping enrichment for media index 0 on page 1 with metadata {'type': 'picture', 'width': 517, 'height': 108, 'info_hashable': '{"height": 108, "type": "picture", "width": 517}', 'page_num': 1} because it was rejected by the LLM provider for 'gpt-4o-2024-11-20'. Full error message: litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - You uploaded an unsupported image. Please make sure your image has of one the following formats: ['png', 'jpeg', 'gif', 'webp'].. Received Model Group=gpt-4o-2024-11-20

is there a way to address this issue?

comments.author: dosubot
comments.text:
<!-- Answer -->
This error happens because PaperQA extracts images from PDFs using PyMuPDF and stores them as raw pixmap bytes, but does not convert them to a format accepted by the LLM provider (which only allows png, jpeg, gif, or webp) before enrichment. Some PDFs contain images in formats that GPT-4o rejects, which is why you see this error for only some files and not others. Images extracted via PyPDF are always converted to PNG, so they don't trigger this issue—it's specific to the PyMuPDF path [source](https://github.com/Future-House/paper-qa/pull/1158).

To fix this, you can add a conversion step using Pillow (PIL) right after extracting images with PyMuPDF, before sending them for enrichment. Here’s a minimal example of how you could do this:

```python
from PIL import Image
import io

def pixmap_to_png_bytes(pix):
    img = Image.frombytes("RGB", [pix.width, pix.height], pix.samples)
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    img.save(buf, format="PNG")
    return buf.getvalue()
```

You would call this function instead of `pix.tobytes()` when creating your `ParsedMedia` objects in the PDF parsing logic (likely in `paperqa/readers.py` or wherever PyMuPDF image extraction happens).

If you want a quick workaround without code changes, you can disable multimodal enrichment by setting `parsing.multimodal` to `False` in your config, which will skip image extraction and revert to text-only processing. You can also enable `answer.evidence_text_only_fallback: true` to automatically retry context creation without media if enrichment fails [source](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/cc2e2476-a1b9-410a-8fe6-07750c74db63).

If you want to debug which images are problematic, you can log or inspect the image metadata (type, width, height, etc.) from the error message to see which formats are being rejected.

Let me know if you want a more detailed code snippet or guidance on where to insert this in your codebase.

Hi @satra, with `paper-qa[pypdf]==2026.01.05`, the below code works for me, including enrichment:

```python
from paperqa import Docs, Settings

docs = Docs()
settings = Settings(
    parsing={"parse_pdf": "paperqa_pypdf.parse_pdf_to_pages", "multimodal": True}
)
docname = await docs.aadd(
    "zsae048.pdf",
    title=(
        "Data-driven, generalizable prediction of adolescent sleep disturbances"
        " in the multisite Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study"
    ),
    doi="10.1093/sleep/zsae048",
    settings=settings,
)
(details,) = (d for d in docs.docs.values() if d.docname == docname)
texts = [t for t in docs.texts if t.doc == details]
media = [m for t in texts for m in t.media]
```

Can you give me a Python script that repros your issue?

comments.author: jamesbraza
comments.text:
Hi @satra okay I figured it out. Can you run `pip list | grep -e pypdf -e pdfplumber -e pymupdf` for me?

I think the issue is that:

1. You're using PyPDF reader (`paper-qa-pypdf`)
2. You don't have `pdfplumber` installed, which means `MediaMode.INDIVIDUAL` is being used
3. Apparently in this individual media mode, the image read is not PNG it's something else (possibly JPEG 2000)
4. We are telling OpenAI the image is PNG, but it's some other type, and the model times out

I will fix this. To work around this in the meantime, either:

- Install `pymupdf` via `pip install paper-qa[pymupdf]`. This will circumvent this error by using our PyMuPDF reader.
- Install `pdfplumber` via `pip install paper-qa[pypdf-enhanced]`. This will circumvent this error by using a more featureful PyPDF reader
